note: Every instrument in the RARA legal scope is listed once. Binding instruments carry exact excerpts in legal-texts.json; guidance, draft, process and forthcoming instruments are named so they cannot be mistaken for law. State laws, municipal bylaws, tribunal orders and private standards sit outside this ledger.

instruments.scope: Articles 14, 19 and 21 set the equality, speech and privacy floor that every AI-facing rule has to survive. Articles 14, 19(1)(a) and 21 are quoted.
Identity offences, privacy, data protection, intermediary safe harbour and blocking. Six exact provisions are quoted.

instruments.instrument: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 (as amended in 2026)
instruments.scope: India's first binding AI-specific regime: the definition of synthetically generated information, automated prevention and labelling duties, and the three-hour takedown route. Four exact provisions are quoted.

instruments.regulator: MeitY / Data Protection Board of India
instruments.scope: Consent, children's data, security safeguards, breach intimation, cross-border transfer, Significant Data Fiduciary duties, penalties and the research exemption. Ten exact provisions are quoted.

instruments.regulator: MeitY / Data Protection Board of India
instruments.scope: Security safeguards, breach intimation to the Data Principal and the Board, verifiable parental consent, and the annual DPIA and audit owed by a Significant Data Fiduciary. Five exact provisions are quoted.
Personation, cheating, defamation, voyeurism and forgery, including false electronic records. Five exact provisions are quoted.
Admissibility of electronic records, including the conditions for treating computer output as evidence and the certificate required at admission. Two exact provisions are quoted.

instruments.regulator: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
instruments.scope: Fair dealing, infringement and moral rights around training data and generated likeness. Two exact provisions are quoted.

instruments.regulator: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
instruments.scope: The exclusion of computer programmes and algorithms from patentability, read against AI inventorship. One exact provision is quoted.
Anti-competitive agreements, price fixing and abuse of dominance, including algorithmic coordination. Three exact provisions are quoted.
Misleading advertisements, unfair trade practices and the punishment for a false or misleading advertisement. Three exact provisions are quoted.

instruments.instrument: CERT-In Directions under s. 70B of the IT Act, 2000 (2022)
instruments.scope: Six-hour cyber-incident reporting and 180-day log retention inside India. Two exact provisions are quoted.

instruments.instrument: Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
instruments.scope: Core biometric information cannot be shared or used beyond Aadhaar generation and authentication; other identity information is purpose-limited. Two exact provisions are quoted.
Telecom cyber-security policy, audits and six-hour incident reporting for telecom entities. Two exact provisions are quoted.

instruments.instrument: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Cybersecurity, Technology: Risk, Resilience and Assurance Framework) Directions, 2026
instruments.scope: Board-approved technology and cybersecurity policies, annual review and technology-risk governance for NBFCs. One exact provision is quoted.

instruments.instrument: Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience Framework (CSCRF) for SEBI Regulated Entities, 2024
instruments.regulator: Securities and Exchange Board of India
instruments.scope: Board-approved cybersecurity and cyber resilience policy, graded compliance, SOC and incident reporting for SEBI-regulated entities. One exact provision is quoted.

instruments.instrument: Election Commission of India Directions on Responsible Use and Disclosure of Synthetically Generated Information and AI-Generated Content during Elections, 2025
instruments.scope: Article 324 directions to political parties, candidates and campaign representatives: labels, metadata, a prohibition on misleading synthetic content, three-hour takedown and record-keeping. Three exact provisions are quoted.
Dark-pattern compliance, yearly self-audit and disclosure duties for e-commerce entities. The 2026 amendment is notified but commences on 1 January 2027; one exact provision is quoted.

instruments.instrument: FREE-AI Committee Report – Framework for Responsible and Ethical Enablement of Artificial Intelligence
instruments.scope: Seven sutras and twenty-six recommendations on responsible AI in finance, including entity accountability and board oversight. A committee report with no compliance duty; one exact excerpt is in the documents layer.

instruments.instrument: IRDAI Office Order constituting the Working Group on Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance in the Insurance Sector
instruments.regulator: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
instruments.scope: Constitutes a seven-member working group on AI governance for insurance, with recommendations due within three months. No report or binding AI rule had been published at retrieval; one exact excerpt is in the documents layer.
Seven sutras and six governance pillars. Voluntary guidance: it can shape practice but cannot close a statutory gap.

instruments.instrument: NITI Aayog Approach Document for India: Responsible AI for All, 2021
instruments.scope: Seven responsible-AI principles. A policy approach, not a binding instrument.

instruments.instrument: RBI Draft Guidance on Regulatory Principles for Model Risk Management, 2026
instruments.scope: Enterprise model governance, validation, tiering and continuous oversight for regulated entities. Still a draft; no compliance duty attaches until finalised.

instruments.instrument: SEBI Advisory on Emerging Advanced AI Tools for Vulnerability Detection, 2026
instruments.regulator: Securities and Exchange Board of India
instruments.scope: Advisory on AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and the security posture of regulated securities entities. Advisory, not a closure instrument.
No standalone AI Act is in force. The 2025 guidelines remain voluntary; a draft Bill has not been published.
